prompt:
solution.py is meant to implement the specification below, but it contains several defects. One has been reported: `wrap("a b c", 3)` returns ["a", "b", "c"] instead of ["a b", "c"]. Fix that and every other deviation from the specification. Keep the public names and signatures unchanged and do not change behaviour the specification requires.

Specification: Implement `wrap(text, width)` in solution.py and return a list of lines. Paragraphs are separated by one or more blank lines (a blank line is empty or holds only whitespace) and are wrapped independently; in the output, consecutive paragraphs are separated by exactly one empty string, and there is no empty string before the first or after the last paragraph. Inside a paragraph, words are maximal runs of non-whitespace characters; all whitespace, single newlines included, only separates words. Lines are filled greedily: a word joins the current line when the line, one space and the word together fit within `width`, otherwise it starts a new line. A word longer than `width` always starts on a new line and is cut into chunks of exactly `width` characters, the last chunk possibly shorter; the next word may join that last chunk if it fits. No line has leading or trailing spaces. Text without any word gives []. Raise ValueError when `width` is less than 1.
acceptance: a word that exactly fits stays on the line
paragraphs are separated by exactly one empty string
the word after an over-long word may join its last chunk
